front_matter.preface: This volume constitutes the official Tangkhul section of the Linguistic Survey of India (Vol. III, Part II), surveyed by Sir George Abraham Grierson and printed at the Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing, Calcutta, in 1903. It preserves the earliest comprehensive comparative grammatical analysis, standard vocabulary list, and translated textual specimens of the Tangkhul Naga language as spoken in the Ukhrul subdivision of Manipur.

chapters.summary: Vowels, consonants, diphthongs, and glottal tone stops introduced by W. Pettigrew.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Vowels: a, ā, e, ē, i, ī, o, ō, u, ū. Consonants: k, kh, ng, ch, chh, j, t, th, n, p, ph, m, y, r, l, w, s, sh, h. Kakhalat kashak shiyan eina tui khangatei kachung lei.

grammar_points: Macron diacritic marks long vowel quantity (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū).
Aspiration contrasts phonemically in initial plosives: k vs kh, t vs th, p vs ph.

chapters.title: The Noun System & Case Inflections
chapters.summary: Natural gender indicators, plural formations, and postpositional case endings.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon bing: mayarnaona (nominative), mayarnaoli (accusative/dative), mayarnaowui (genitive), mayarnaoeina (instrumental/ablative). Chitharan shiyan kakhane: si (dog), siva (bitch), simayār (male dog).
chapters.english_translation: Case suffixes attached to nominal stems: -na (nominative/agentive), -li (dative/objective), -wui (genitive/possessive), -eina (instrumental/ablative). Gender markers: -va (female) and -mayār (male).
grammar_points: Agentive suffix -na is obligatory for subjects of transitive verbs.
Plurality is formed by adding -bing or -binda to nominal bases.

chapters.title: Verb Conjugation, Tenses & Moods

chapters.title: Specimen I: The Parable of the Prodigal Son (Complete)
chapters.summary: Authentic full-text translation of Luke 15:11-32 in Tangkhul Naga with verse-by-verse gloss.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
11. Mi akhali mayarnaowon khani leiyi.
12. Kakhani chiwui ngachaili kakhanao china aishavaali kahang, 'Ava, ramwui kashikhavai ngashan iwui khavai thali ili milu.' Chiwui vang aishavana aram athum khaniwui ngachaili ngashanserie.
13. Zingkum kachung mathaloikhalang kakhanao china aishapup sanglaga kashak ramli vashitserie, chitharan aphasa kakhano awui vang phasa ngalung khayai eina khamatai thotna.
14. Ana atam sashidaran ram chithuili haora kapha thotna; chitharan a kacham thotna.
15. Chiwui vang a vashitlaga chiwui ramwui mi akhali phungphada leiyi; ana ali awui lili hok kashukhavai ngasikseriya.
16. Chitharan ana hokna shakhavai theichon chieina phasa vashikhavai ningkachon leiyi; chalieikha mi akhana ali mimana.
17. Kha ana awui ning kazil chitharan ana kahang, 'Iva wui ngavaia mi kachungkhana kachak mathaloikhalang thari, kha i hiwui phasa ngalung kazata eina thiyei!'
18. 'I ngakhokda iva wui lili vara, ana ali hangra: Ava, Kazingramli kala na makhaingalina i yor kasa mi thotna.'
19. 'Chiwui vang nawui nao kachi tui shiyan katha mavana; ili nawui ngavaia mi akha gaka thada sanglu.'
20. Chithālaga a ngakhokda aishava wui lili vayi. Kha a kashakli leitharan aishavana ali theilaga kachan pamei, chithālaga ngathimlaga akukli chukda kachamseriya.
21. Nao china ali kahang, 'Ava, Kazingramli kala na makhaingalina i yor kasa mi thotna; nawui nao kachi tui shiyan katha mavana.'
22. Kha aishavana awui ngavaia mi bingli kahang, 'Kaphāmei kachon sanglalu, ali khonlu; kala awui pangyali chap sanglu, awui pheili khokhop sanglu.'
23. 'Kala se phapharo shithalu, ngasotlu; ithum sashilaga mathaseru.'
24. 'Iwui nao hi thida leikha kazing thotna, themda leikha theikhuiraser.' Chitharan athum mathapameiser.
25. Chitharan awui mayarnaowon kakhara a lili leiyi; a ngateilaga shim mathatungda leikhara laa khavai kala ngakhum kaphei khangazip tharan a kashana.
26. Ana ngavaia mi akhali hoklaga, 'Hi khi thotno?' da ngahangyei.
27. Ana ali kahang, 'Nawui nanao vashungser, nawui avana se phapharo shithiser, ana phasa katha theikhuira tharan.'
28. Chiwui vang a kachuk thotna, a shimli ungkhavai ningkachon maleimana; chiwui vang aishava vashitlaga ali kahangyei.
29. Ana ngashitda aishavaali kahang, 'Theilu, kum hiya thada i nali ngavaiyei, nawui tui kachikha mamatai-mana; chithakha iwui azeishinao bingli ngasotda sashikhavai senao akha gaka ili mimana.'
30. 'Kha nawui nao khamatai thotna ngalanao bingli nawui ram shiser china vang se phapharo shithimina!'
31. Ana ali kahang, 'Nao, na i eina kapam thotna, iwui ot phasa shishapup nawuina.'
32. 'Kha mathada ngasotkhavai shiyan phamei; nanao hi thida leikha kazing thotna, themda leikha theikhuiraser.'
chapters.english_translation:
11. A certain man had two sons:
12. And the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me.' And he divided unto them his living.
13. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
14. And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
15. And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
16. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
17. And when he came to himself, he said, 'How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!'
18. 'I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,'
19. 'And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.'
20. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
21. And the son said unto him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.'
22. But the father said to his servants, 'Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:'
23. 'And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:'
24. 'For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found.' And they began to be merry.
25. Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing.
26. And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
27. And he said unto him, 'Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.'
28. And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.
29. And he answering said to his father, 'Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:'
30. 'But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.'
31. And he said unto him, 'Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.'
32. 'It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.'

he divided unto them his living. 13. And not many days after the younger
son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and
there wasted his substance with riotous living. 14. And when he had
spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be
in want. 15. And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that
country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine. 16. And he would
fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no
man gave unto him. 17. And when he came to himself, he said, 'How many
hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I
perish with hunger!' 18. 'I will arise and go to my father, and will say
unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,' 19.

servants.' 20. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet
a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and
fell on his neck, and kissed him. 21. And the son said unto him,

worthy to be called thy son.' 22. But the father said to his servants,

hand, and shoes on his feet:' 23. 'And bring hither the fatted calf, and
kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:' 24. 'For this my son was dead,

merry. 25. Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew

the servants, and asked what these things meant. 27. And he said unto

unto him, 'Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.'
32. 'It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy
brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.'

excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Naga hi Manipur ramwui kaphung zanshorli kapam tui thotna. Ukhrul kaphung hi Tangkhul tuiwui phungreitang thada shiyan kashakna. Tui hi Tibeto-Burman wui Naga-Kuki tui ngachaili shangserna.
excerpts.translation_en: The Tangkhul Nagas inhabit the eastern hill tracts of Manipur State. The village of Ukhrul serves as the central cultural and linguistic standard. The language belongs to the Naga-Bodo / Tibeto-Burman linguistic stock.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Phonology and the Roman Alphabet
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Vowels: a, ā, e, ē, i, ī, o, ō, u, ū. Consonants: k, kh, ng, ch, chh, j, t, th, n, p, ph, m, y, r, l, w, s, sh, h. Kakhalat kashak shiyan eina tui khangatei kachung lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Vowel inventory with phonemic length distinctions: short and long vowels. Consonantal series with aspirated stops (kh, th, ph, chh). Syllable-final consonants and tonal inflections alter word significations.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: The Noun System & Case Inflections
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon bing: mayarnaona (nominative), mayarnaoli (accusative/dative), mayarnaowui (genitive), mayarnaoeina (instrumental/ablative). Chitharan shiyan kakhane: si (dog), siva (bitch), simayār (male dog).
excerpts.translation_en: Case suffixes attached to nominal stems: -na (nominative/agentive), -li (dative/objective), -wui (genitive/possessive), -eina (instrumental/ablative). Gender markers: -va (female) and -mayār (male).

excerpts.tangkhul_text: Kaphā (good), kakhui (bitter), kacham (poor). Comparison: kaphāmei (better), pamei (best). Numerals: akha (1), khani (2), kathum (3), mati (4), phangā (5), tharuk (6), shini (7), chishat (8), chiko (9), thakharā / magā (10). Pronouns: i (I), na (thou), a (he/she).
excerpts.translation_en: Descriptive adjectives are derived using prefix ka-. Comparison is marked with -mei. Cardinal numerals from 1 to 10. Personal pronouns: 1st person 'i', 2nd person 'na', 3rd person 'a'; plurals: ithum, nathum, athum.

excerpts.tangkhul_text: I sai (I do, present), i sada / i theiser (past), i sara (future). Imperative: salu (do!), theilu (see!). Negative: masa-mana (does not do), mathei-mana (does not see). Causative: -sak (sasaku).
excerpts.translation_en: Verbs conjugate through tense suffixes: present -ei/-i, past -ser/-da, future -ra. Imperative forms take suffix -lu. Negation frames the verbal root with prefix ma- and suffix -mana. Causation is expressed with -sak.

excerpts.tangkhul_text:
11. Mi akhali mayarnaowon khani leiyi.
12. Kakhani chiwui ngachaili kakhanao china aishavaali kahang, 'Ava, ramwui kashikhavai ngashan iwui khavai thali ili milu.' Chiwui vang aishavana aram athum khaniwui ngachaili ngashanserie.
13. Zingkum kachung mathaloikhalang kakhanao china aishapup sanglaga kashak ramli vashitserie, chitharan aphasa kakhano awui vang phasa ngalung khayai eina khamatai thotna.
14. Ana atam sashidaran ram chithuili haora kapha thotna; chitharan a kacham thotna.
15. Chiwui vang a vashitlaga chiwui ramwui mi akhali phungphada leiyi; ana ali awui lili hok kashukhavai ngasikseriya.
16. Chitharan ana hokna shakhavai theichon chieina phasa vashikhavai ningkachon leiyi; chalieikha mi akhana ali mimana.
17. Kha ana awui ning kazil chitharan ana kahang, 'Iva wui ngavaia mi kachungkhana kachak mathaloikhalang thari, kha i hiwui phasa ngalung kazata eina thiyei!'
18. 'I ngakhokda iva wui lili vara, ana ali hangra: Ava, Kazingramli kala na makhaingalina i yor kasa mi thotna.'
19. 'Chiwui vang nawui nao kachi tui shiyan katha mavana; ili nawui ngavaia mi akha gaka thada sanglu.'
20. Chithālaga a ngakhokda aishava wui lili vayi. Kha a kashakli leitharan aishavana ali theilaga kachan pamei, chithālaga ngathimlaga akukli chukda kachamseriya.
21. Nao china ali kahang, 'Ava, Kazingramli kala na makhaingalina i yor kasa mi thotna; nawui nao kachi tui shiyan katha mavana.'
22. Kha aishavana awui ngavaia mi bingli kahang, 'Kaphāmei kachon sanglalu, ali khonlu; kala awui pangyali chap sanglu, awui pheili khokhop sanglu.'
23. 'Kala se phapharo shithalu, ngasotlu; ithum sashilaga mathaseru.'
24. 'Iwui nao hi thida leikha kazing thotna, themda leikha theikhuiraser.' Chitharan athum mathapameiser.
25. Chitharan awui mayarnaowon kakhara a lili leiyi; a ngateilaga shim mathatungda leikhara laa khavai kala ngakhum kaphei khangazip tharan a kashana.
26. Ana ngavaia mi akhali hoklaga, 'Hi khi thotno?' da ngahangyei.
27. Ana ali kahang, 'Nawui nanao vashungser, nawui avana se phapharo shithiser, ana phasa katha theikhuira tharan.'
28. Chiwui vang a kachuk thotna, a shimli ungkhavai ningkachon maleimana; chiwui vang aishava vashitlaga ali kahangyei.
29. Ana ngashitda aishavaali kahang, 'Theilu, kum hiya thada i nali ngavaiyei, nawui tui kachikha mamatai-mana; chithakha iwui azeishinao bingli ngasotda sashikhavai senao akha gaka ili mimana.'
30. 'Kha nawui nao khamatai thotna ngalanao bingli nawui ram shiser china vang se phapharo shithimina!'
31. Ana ali kahang, 'Nao, na i eina kapam thotna, iwui ot phasa shishapup nawuina.'
32. 'Kha mathada ngasotkhavai shiyan phamei; nanao hi thida leikha kazing thotna, themda leikha theikhuiraser.'

11. A certain man had two sons:
12. And the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me.' And he divided unto them his living.
13. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
14. And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
15. And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
16. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
17. And when he came to himself, he said, 'How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!'
18. 'I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,'
19. 'And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.'
20. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
21. And the son said unto him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.'
22. But the father said to his servants, 'Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:'
23. 'And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:'
24. 'For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found.' And they began to be merry.
25. Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing.
26. And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
27. And he said unto him, 'Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.'
28. And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.
29. And he answering said to his father, 'Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:'
30. 'But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.'
31. And he said unto him, 'Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.'
32. 'It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.'
